# Additions to Esther Chapter 2 (Addition B) — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther B
**Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_002_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Decision

Addition B provides the full text of the genocidal decree, which the Hebrew Esther only summarizes. The Greek author has composed it in the high bureaucratic style of royal correspondence: measured, self-congratulatory, and utterly murderous. The translation must preserve this terrible irony — the language of benevolent governance deployed to authorize massacre. LOGOS provides the formal register; PNEUMA contributes the rhetorical momentum of the edict's self-justifying logic. The letter must read as an authentic royal document.

---

*[Addition B: Full text of King Artaxerxes's edict against the Jews. Inserted after Hebrew Esther 3:13.]*

**1** The following is a copy of the letter: "The Great King Artaxerxes writes to the governors of the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces, from India to Ethiopia, and to their subordinate officials, as follows:

**2** Having become master of many nations and obtained lordship over the whole world, I resolved — not lifted up by the arrogance of power, but consistently governing with fairness and a gentle hand —

**3** to establish for my subjects a life of unbroken tranquility, and to make my kingdom peaceful, orderly, and accessible to all — renewing, in short, the peace that all people desire.

**4** When I inquired of my advisors how this goal might be achieved, Haman — who stands foremost among us in wisdom, has proven himself through steadfast goodwill and unwavering loyalty, and holds the second rank in the kingdom —

**5** pointed out to us that there is scattered among all the nations a certain hostile people, whose laws stand contrary to those of every other nation, and who consistently disregard the commands of the king, so that the honorable and efficient administration of our kingdom cannot be brought to completion.

**6** Understanding therefore that this one people is perpetually in opposition to all humanity, conducting itself by alien laws, and hostile to our governance — doing whatever harm it can, and refusing to embrace any of the virtues of civilized society —

**7** we command that all those identified to you in the letters written by Haman — who directs our affairs and stands to us as a second father — together with their wives and children, be utterly destroyed by the swords of their enemies, without pity and without mercy, on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, that is Adar, of the present year,

**8** so that those who have long been hostile, and remain so today, may in a single day descend by violence into Hades — and our affairs hereafter may be left permanently stable and undisturbed."
